youtube.title: A Prime Minister Walked Into the Ocean and Was Never Seen Again | Harold Holt
youtube.description:
On 17 December 1967, Australian Prime Minister Harold Holt, 59 and a keen spearfisher, went swimming at Cheviot Beach near Portsea, Victoria, with friends. The surf was large and his companions thought it too dangerous; Holt swam out into the turbulence and disappeared. One of the largest search operations in Australian history found no trace, and his body was never recovered. World leaders including US President Lyndon Johnson attended his memorial service in Melbourne. Theories followed, including a 1983 claim that he was a Chinese spy collected by submarine, which his widow Zara dismissed. In 2005, Victoria's State Coroner found that he took an unnecessary risk and drowned. A Melbourne swimming centre was later named in his honour.

📂 Case File #030: The Prime Minister Who Vanished

Sources: Wikipedia, "Disappearance of Harold Holt" and its citations (2005 coronial finding); Smithsonian Magazine, "The Prime Minister Who Disappeared".
